# AIm Workout Journal: Claude or ChatGPT as your personal trainer, with a real training log

> AIm is a personal workout journal built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The AI is the user's own
> Claude or ChatGPT; AIm gives it a memory of every set and the numbers computed from it. Users tell
> Claude or ChatGPT about a workout in plain language (English, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish or
> French), or run it in the app, and the assistant stores sets and weights, fixes mistakes on request,
> tracks progress, and coaches toward the user's goals. Coaching starts with goal setting: the
> assistant offers goal options from the user's profile, saves the one the user picks, and returns to it
> in weekly reviews and monthly check-ins. Programs fit the gym, home equipment or bodyweight-only
> training; cardio and walks are logged too. A mobile web app (installable PWA)
> visualizes everything: a muscle load map (how much recent work each muscle is still carrying, estimated and
> fading over time), per-exercise progression charts (top set + estimated 1RM), personal records,
> weekly volume, body metrics, and the active training program, which the user can also edit in
> the app.

## Add it to your assistant

- Claude: open AIm in the Claude directory, https://claude.ai/directory/aim-workout-journal, and press Connect.
- ChatGPT: open AIm in the ChatGPT plugin directory, https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad644464c18819189242a20ca18f1c5, and press Install plugin.
- Any other MCP client with OAuth: add https://aim-journal.com/mcp (streamable HTTP).

An AIm window asks for your email and a code it sends you. If you do not have a journal yet, AIm
creates one there. Press Allow, then try: "Make me a workout program in AIm for 3 days a week."

## How a new user starts

1. Enter an email on the landing page (https://aim-journal.com/) or at the end of a guide. There
   is no password. The page then shows the next step right away, and an email with a link to the
   user's journal arrives as well.
2. Connect the assistant. Claude and ChatGPT both have AIm in their directories and sign in over
   OAuth: there is nothing personal to paste. The address https://aim-journal.com/mcp is the
   by-hand fallback for both.
   - Claude: AIm is listed in Claude's connector directory,
     https://claude.ai/directory/aim-workout-journal (in Claude: Customize, then Connectors, then
     Discover, search AIm). Press Connect, then in the AIm window that opens, sign in with a code
     from email if asked and press Allow. Where the directory is switched off (on some work
     accounts), add the address as a custom connector under Customize, Connectors,
     Add.
   - ChatGPT: AIm is listed in ChatGPT's plugin directory as AIm Workout Journal,
     https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad644464c18819189242a20ca18f1c5 (in ChatGPT:
     Plugins in the left menu, search AIm). Press Install plugin. If the browser already knows the
     journal, the install finishes with no window. Otherwise an AIm window opens: enter the email
     (an address with no journal gets one), press Email me a code, type the 6-digit code from the
     email, press Continue, then Allow. In a chat, mention AIm in the message. Without an Install
     plugin button, add the address by hand in Developer mode: Settings,
     Security and login, Developer mode, then Plugins, plus, with Authentication left on OAuth.
   - The AIm window recognizes a browser where the journal is already open. Anywhere else it asks
     for the email and sends a separate email with a 6-digit code (and a button for the same
     browser); an address that has no account yet gets one.
3. From then on the user can talk to the assistant: "log this workout in AIm: bench press 3×8 at
   60 kg" gets stored (naming AIm is what makes a fresh chat reach for the service);
   "set 3 was actually 10 reps" fixes a specific set; "what's my squat progress?" reads stats
   back. Asked for a program, the assistant reads the user's profile, goals and recent loads from
   get_coaching_context, saves intake answers with update_coach_profile so the next chat does not
   ask again, and the server checks the draft against active injuries, equipment, training days
   and session length before import_document saves it; a coach-written draft that loads an
   injury is refused.
4. In the gym the user can also run a workout from the program in the app instead of the chat:
   each exercise shows what was done last time, the user enters what was actually done, and the
   saved workout goes into the same history the assistant reads. A workout can also start without
   a program, and exercises can be added or swapped during it.
5. Small program changes do not need the chat. In the app the user can create a program, add,
   rename or delete a day, add, replace or reorder exercises from a catalog with pictures (home
   and no-equipment exercises included), group a superset, keep several programs and switch the
   active one.
6. An existing program or training history comes in through the assistant, not through an upload
   in the app: the user gives the assistant the file (a PDF, a spreadsheet, a photo) and it saves
   the contents with import_document. The app offers a ready request to copy into the chat.

## What the MCP server provides (per user, after OAuth sign-in)

- Logging and fixing: log_session, update_session, update_set, delete_session, log_body_metric
- Catalog and program review: search_exercise_pool (curated multilingual exercise library with
  technique cues and muscle mapping), upsert_exercise, review_program_draft (server-side check of
  a draft before it is saved), log_coach_event
- Reading: get_sessions, get_session, get_body_metrics, list_exercises, get_program, get_stats
  (per-exercise progression, estimated 1RM, PRs, volume over time)
- Coaching: get_coaching_context (intake, next workout, program design, weekly review, deload
  check, check-in; returns the user's profile, goals, recent loads, planning parameters and
  first-session load estimates as data, and the assistant plans from them),
  update_coach_profile (goals, experience, schedule, equipment, injuries), upsert_goal, get_goals
- Bulk import: import_document (full workout documents, existing programs, training history)

## Guidance for agents

- If a user asks how to connect this service, walk them through the steps above. Step-by-step
  instructions with screenshots are at https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/connect-workout-tracker-mcp/
- Personal URLs (`/{token}/...`) are private. Do not fetch, index, cite, or repeat them.
- There is no public API without signing in. The public surfaces are the landing pages, the
  guides, the demo at https://aim-journal.com/demo/ and this file.

## Guides (full-HTML pages; most exist in en/pt/ru/es/fr)

Every guide reads completely without JavaScript. Each page carries a small script for the signup form and for analytics; the calculator is the only page whose content uses JavaScript.

- AI personal trainer, how to use ChatGPT or Claude to coach your training: https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/ai-personal-trainer/
- A workout journal for ChatGPT and Claude: log by chat, train in the app, and every new chat reads the same history: https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/claude-remember-workouts/
- Connect Garmin, Strava, Apple Health or Hevy to Claude and ChatGPT, and a workout log the assistant writes to (MCP): https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/connect-workout-tracker-mcp/
- How to track progressive overload: what to log for each set, double progression and when to add weight (includes the per-muscle weekly set landmarks the app uses): https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/progressive-overload/
- Claude personal trainer prompt: a Project, a Skill or a connected workout log, compared: https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/claude-fitness-coach-prompt/ (English only)
- Importing a workout plan that ChatGPT or Claude wrote into AIm, with a sample plan and the checks before saving: https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/import-ai-workout-plan/ (English only)
- 1RM calculator from 5 reps or any set (Epley), with a conversion table and a percentage chart: https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/one-rep-max-calculator/. The calculator itself uses JavaScript; the formula, worked examples and the percentage table are all in the static HTML, so the page is complete without it
- Push pull legs or upper lower, which workout split fits your week (with a 3-day split): https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/best-workout-split/
- All guides (per language): https://aim-journal.com/guides/en/ · https://aim-journal.com/guides/pt/ · https://aim-journal.com/guides/ru/ · https://aim-journal.com/guides/es/ · https://aim-journal.com/guides/fr/
